title: Least squares
goal: Explain why the normal equations give the line with the smallest squared error, and solve them.

squared-error.claim: Least squares picks the line that makes the sum of squared vertical errors as small as possible; squaring makes every error count positively and weighs large errors more.
squared-error.probe: Why does least squares square the errors before adding them, instead of adding them as they are? Give two reasons.
rubric: Says that plain errors of opposite sign cancel, so their sum can be zero for a bad line
Says that squaring weighs large errors more than small ones (or that it makes the error smooth to minimise)
squared-error.transfer_probe: A colleague proposes minimising the sum of absolute errors instead. Name one way the fitted line could differ.
why_chain: Errors of opposite sign cancel in a plain sum.
A square is never negative and grows fast.

normal-equations.claim: Setting the gradient of the squared error to zero gives the normal equations, A^T A beta = A^T y: the residual is orthogonal to every column of A.
normal-equations.probe: Starting from the squared error ||A beta - y||^2, derive the normal equations, and say what they mean about the residual.
rubric: Takes the gradient, 2 A^T (A beta - y), and sets it to zero
Arrives at A^T A beta = A^T y
Says the residual A beta - y is orthogonal to the columns of A
normal-equations.transfer_probe: For a fit through the origin (one column, x), write the normal equation and solve it for the slope.
why_chain: A smooth function is smallest where its gradient is zero.
A^T r = 0 says r has no component along any column.

solve-the-system.claim: To fit y = a x + b, stack the design matrix A = [x 1] and solve the 2x2 system A^T A beta = A^T y; beta[0] is the slope and beta[1] the intercept.
solve-the-system.probe: Fit y = a x + b to the points (0, 1), (1, 3), (2, 5). Show the design matrix, the system you solve, and the slope and intercept.
rubric: Writes the design matrix with rows [x_i 1]
solve-the-system.transfer_probe: Fit y = a x^2 + b x + c by the same method: what is the design matrix, and how big is the system?
why_chain: The normal equations are square, so they can be solved directly.

practice.problem_frame: Fit a line to three or four given points by forming and solving the normal equations by hand.
practice.verify: Check that the residuals sum to zero and are orthogonal to the x column.
